validated_work_order.understanding:
Issue #61 bundles eight follow-ups from PR #59 (merged 2026-10-04). Six are e2e-test hygiene; two are real defects in shipped code. I re-verified every claim against the code and executed the ones that were falsifiable.

Review 1 (menu introspection does not auto-wait) is real: _openNthScheduleMenu returns a lazy Locator that consumers read with count()/allTextContents(), neither of which retries. Review 2 (index-vs-payee incoherence) is real as written — payee locators are built and asserted toHaveCount(1), then two assertions use raw indices 2 and 3. Review 3 ([AI] title) is not a change to this repository; PR #59 is merged, 0fb77b4 already carries [AI], and .github/** is a forbidden path. Review 4 (duplicated $send('query',...) envelope) is real — two byte-for-byte identical 12-key objects, each in its own page.evaluate with its own window cast. Review 5 (redundant open/dismiss/re-open) is real.

QA 1 (exhausted recurrence still offers Skip; silent no-op) is real and I REPRODUCED IT BY EXECUTION: a scratch spec showed that for a recur of {start: today, endMode: 'after_n_occurrences', endOccurrences: 1}, scheduleIsRecurring returns true while getNextDateAfter returns null. The primitive and its exhausted case already exist and are already tested; the UI asks a weaker question than the write does.

QA 2 (two concurrent skips) does not hold as diagnosed and is dropped. runMutator is sequential(_runMutator) over one module-level queue, skip-next-date is registered mutator(undoable(...)), and runHandler routes every mutating handler through that queue — on the API path too. What QA observed is precisely what serialised execution produces.

QA 3 (React controlled/uncontrolled warnings) is real with a single-line cause: useScheduleEdit's nullable name reaches Input unguarded, while the payee (159) and account (175) inputs in the same file already carry the || '' guard.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Three distinct causes. (1) The UI and the write ask different questions: four skip-eligibility sites call scheduleIsRecurring ('is this a recurrence at all?') while setNextDate asks the strictly stronger 'does getNextDateAfter return a date?', which is false once the recurrence is exhausted. Demonstrated by execution — for an after_n_occurrences-1 recur starting today the first returns true and the second null. PR #59 introduced the weaker predicate, so the UI offers an action the server drops. (2) useScheduleEdit's field state is nullable by type and ScheduleEditForm renders fields.name into a controlled Input without the || '' guard its siblings already have — the only unguarded nullable string pass-through in the file. (3) The e2e page model returns a lazy Locator to callers reading it with non-retrying Playwright calls, while the test grew a second index-based path alongside the payee-based one, plus a duplicated AQL envelope and a redundant open/dismiss cycle.
validated_work_order.approach: Three changes in dependency order. (A) Add scheduleIsSkippable(dateCond, nextDate) to loot-core shared/schedules.ts: scheduleIsRecurring(dateCond) && getNextDateAfter(dateCond, nextDate) != null, short-circuiting false on a null/undefined nextDate. It reuses getNextDateAfter rather than reimplementing occurrence logic, so the UI predicate and the setNextDate write are driven by the same function and cannot drift — that reuse is the fix, not an implementation detail. New function rather than a widened scheduleIsRecurring because three callers read that predicate inverted for Complete and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it for preview expansion. Then swap the four skip-eligibility call sites, passing the row's next_date; all four already select '*'. (B) value={fields.name} becomes value={fields.name || ''} at ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134, matching lines 159 and 175. The reducer's initial null is left alone: it is read for truthiness where null and '' are equally falsy. (C) e2e hygiene: await expect(menu).toBeVisible() once inside _openNthScheduleMenu so all three consumers inherit the wait; widen the row parameter of three helpers to number | Locator so the test's existing payee locators replace raw indices; hoist a module-level Node-side aqlQuery<T> owning the duplicated $send('query') envelope, with the split-transfer test's browser-side queries moving out through it (page.evaluate is serialised and cannot close over a Node binding); delete the redundant open/count-0/Escape block; add a console assertion modelled on command-bar.test.ts, filtered by regex to the two React controlled/uncontrolled warning texts.

alternatives_considered.approach: Follow QA 1's stated remedy: drop setNextDate's `newNextDate != null` guard and surface the no-op to the caller instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the wrong layer. The null guard is load-bearing — getNextDateAfter legitimately returns null for an exhausted recurrence and an existing test asserts it — so removing it would write null into schedules_next_date. The UI needs eligibility up front regardless, since a client cannot learn from an absent error that an action was dropped.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 1 by teaching scheduleIsRecurring itself to check for a remaining occurrence, leaving the four call sites untouched.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Smaller diff, wrong answer. Three sites read the predicate inverted for Complete and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it for preview expansion, where 'is this recurring?' is the right question. One predicate cannot serve both.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 2 as reported, with a compare-and-swap on schedules_next_date keyed on the next_date that was read.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is no race for it to close — runMutator is a single serialised queue, so the second skip legitimately reads the first's committed write. A CAS would make a user's second deliberate skip do nothing and silently lose a client retry.

alternatives_considered.approach: For review 2 and 5, delete the payee locators and the index-independence comment and keep the raw indices, on the grounds that they are correct today and fail loudly on drift.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer already granted the indices are correct; the objection is that the comment claims a guarantee the test does not keep. Deleting the locators removes the better mechanism to satisfy the weaker one.

alternatives_considered.approach: For review 4, hoist only the 12-key envelope object to module scope and spread it into both page.evaluate callbacks.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not work. A page.evaluate callback is serialised into the browser and cannot reference a Node-scope binding, so the spread would throw a ReferenceError. Deduplication requires a Node-side function that owns its own evaluate.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 3 in useScheduleEdit by seeding the reducer's initial state with name: '' instead of null.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A wider edit with no behavioural gain — name is read for truthiness where '' and null are both falsy — and it touches the state contract rather than the render site, where lines 159 and 175 already establish the codebase's convention.

validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no debate to arbitrate. plan/critique.json is an empty object — the critic wrote nothing — so this council's third round is effectively a single-planner plan that I audited rather than arbitrated between. I am recording that plainly rather than manufacturing agreement. Where the final work order differs from the proposal, it is my edit.

What the brief's rejection changed, and what I checked about it. The brief records a rejected v1 with four required corrections, and the proposal (v2) claims all four are addressed. I verified each against the code rather than taking the claim.

(1) v1 claimed AC-1's exhausted fixture 'cannot be built through the UI'. That was FALSE, and the proposal correctly reversed it. I confirmed it independently twice. Structurally: RecurringSchedulePicker.tsx does render repeat_end_dropdown (:442), #end_occurrences (:454) and #end_date (:468), and Apply at :579 calls onSave(unparseConfig(config)) through ScheduleEditForm's set-field date dispatch. ScheduleEditModal.tsx:52's endMode: 'never' is the initial value the picker overwrites, not a constraint — the previous round read it as a hardcode and built a whole criterion on the misreading. Behaviourally, I executed the resulting config: start seeded to today with after_n_occurrences 1 gives getNextDateAfter(today) === null, exactly the exhausted state. I also note the previous review cited the picker at components/schedules/ when it lives at components/select/ — a sign that round's reading was hurried. I kept the proposal's browser-path AC-1 and added the exact control ids so QA is not left hunting.

(2) v1 marked AC-5/6/7 verify:'test' while citing Playwright files no CI job runs, which qa.md makes unpassable since a verify:'test' criterion must cite 'ci'. The proposal restated all three as browser criteria — the right repair — but not unaltered; see below.

(3) v1's AC-4 demanded 'no other console error or warning' while its own implementation narrowed the e2e filter to two React warning texts. The proposal fixed it in the right direction, and AC-4 now states explicitly that it is not a claim dev-mode console is otherwise silent.

(4) v1 claimed reproduced:false because node_modules was absent — a reason, not a reproduction. node_modules is present now; I ran schedules.test.ts (80 passing) and the scratch reproduction, so reproduced is true on evidence.

My own edits, which are neither the critic's nor the brief's.

I dropped two of the seven acceptance criteria. The proposal's AC-5 duplicated its AC-4 almost word for word — both said 'opening the schedule edit modal logs neither of the two named React warnings', both verify:'browser', same how_to_verify.
